question: What is the maximum distance the danger zone can extend from the front bumper of a school bus?
explanation: The manual states the danger zones may extend as much as 30 feet from the front bumper, with the first 10 feet being the most dangerous.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1

question: Which area around a school bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars?
choice_a: The left side of the bus
choice_d: The right side of the bus
explanation: The manual states the area to the left of the bus is always considered dangerous because of passing cars.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1

question: When properly adjusted, the outside left and right side flat mirrors should allow the driver to see how far behind the bus?
explanation: The manual states the flat mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see 200 feet or 4 bus lengths behind the bus.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1

question: Depending on the length and width of the bus, how far can the blind spot behind a school bus extend?
explanation: The manual states the blind spot behind the bus extends 50 to 150 feet and could extend up to 400 feet depending on the length and width of the bus.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-1

question: Where are the outside left and right side convex mirrors located?
choice_d: Inside the bus above the windshield
explanation: The manual states the convex mirrors are located below the outside flat mirrors.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-2

question: What is one purpose of the outside left and right side crossover mirrors?
choice_a: To monitor passenger activity inside the bus
choice_b: To view traffic 200 feet behind the bus
choice_c: To see the front bumper danger zone area not visible by direct vision
explanation: The manual states the crossover mirrors are used to see the front bumper danger zone directly in front of the bus that is not visible by direct vision.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-2

question: What is the overhead inside rearview mirror primarily used for?
choice_a: Viewing the danger zone in front of the bus
choice_b: Checking the rear tires touching the ground
choice_c: Monitoring passenger activity inside the bus
choice_d: Viewing traffic approaching from the rear
explanation: The manual states the overhead inside rearview mirror is used to monitor passenger activity inside the bus; exterior side mirrors, not this mirror, must be used to monitor approaching rear traffic.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-3

question: According to the manual, more students are killed each year in which circumstance?
choice_a: While getting on or off a school bus
choice_b: As passengers inside a moving school bus
choice_c: While walking to school without a bus
choice_d: In car accidents unrelated to the bus
explanation: The manual states more students are killed while getting on or off a school bus each year than are killed as passengers inside a school bus.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-3

question: If equipped, the alternating flashing amber warning lights should be activated at least how far (or how many seconds) before the school bus stop?
explanation: The manual states to activate alternating flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet or approximately 5-10 seconds before the school bus stop.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-3

question: About how far, or how many seconds, before pulling over should the driver turn on the right turn signal indicator?
explanation: The manual states to turn on the right turn signal indicator about 100-300 feet or approximately 3-5 seconds before pulling over.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-3

question: When stopping at a designated school bus stop, the front bumper should come to a stop at least how far from the students?
explanation: The manual states to bring the school bus to a full stop with the front bumper at least 10 feet away from students at the designated stop.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-3

question: What should be turned on while loading students in the dark?
explanation: The manual states students should board slowly, in single file, using the handrail, and the dome light should be on while loading in the dark.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-4

question: After exiting the bus during an on-route unloading stop, students should walk how far away from the side of the bus, to a position where the driver can plainly see them?
explanation: The manual states to tell students to exit the bus and walk at least 10 feet away from the side of the bus to a position where the driver can plainly see all students.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-4

question: When students must cross the roadway in front of the bus, they should walk to a location at least how far in front of the right corner of the bumper?
explanation: The manual states students should walk to a location at least 10 feet in front of the right corner of the bumper, while remaining away from the front of the bus.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-4

question: During a post-trip inspection, special attention should be paid to mechanical/operational problems with which items unique to school buses?
choice_a: The fuel gauge and tire pressure
choice_b: Mirror systems, flashing warning lamps, and stop signal arms
explanation: The manual states to give special attention during post-trip inspection to items unique to school buses: mirror systems, flashing warning lamps and stop signal arms.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-6

question: Which of the following requires a mandatory evacuation of the school bus?
choice_d: The bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing
explanation: The manual lists mandatory evacuation conditions, including that the bus is stalled on or adjacent to a railroad-highway crossing.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-6

question: A safe place for evacuated students should be at least how far off the road, in the direction of oncoming traffic?
explanation: The manual states a safe place will be at least 100 feet off the road in the direction of oncoming traffic, to keep students from being hit by debris.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-7

question: If there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials, students should be led upwind of the bus at least how far?
explanation: The manual states to lead students upwind of the bus at least 300 feet if there is a risk from spilled hazardous materials.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-7

question: When possible, how many responsible, older student assistants should be assigned to each emergency exit?
explanation: The manual states that, when possible, two responsible, older student assistants should be assigned to each emergency exit.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-7

question: A passive railroad-highway crossing is one that:
choice_a: Does not have any type of traffic control device
choice_b: Has flashing red lights and gates
choice_d: Is used only by freight trains
explanation: The manual states a passive crossing does not have any type of traffic control device, and the decision to proceed rests entirely with the driver.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-8

question: At a railroad-highway crossing, the school bus should stop no closer than how many feet, and no farther than how many feet, from the nearest rail?
choice_a: No closer than 10 feet, no farther than 40 feet
choice_b: No closer than 25 feet, no farther than 75 feet
choice_c: No closer than 20 feet, no farther than 60 feet
choice_d: No closer than 15 feet, no farther than 50 feet
explanation: The manual states to stop no closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail, where you have the best view of the tracks.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9

question: When approaching a railroad-highway crossing, hazard lights should be activated approximately how far before the crossing?
explanation: The manual states to activate hazard lights approximately 200 feet before the crossing to make your intentions known.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-9

question: The Department of Transportation requires antilock braking systems (ABS) on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies) built on or after:
explanation: The manual states the DOT requires ABS on air brake vehicles (trucks, buses, trailers and converter dollies) built on or after March 1, 1998.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-10

question: When braking a school bus equipped with ABS in an emergency situation, the driver should:
explanation: The manual states that in emergency braking, the driver should not pump the brakes on a bus equipped with ABS.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-10

question: A school bus can have a tail swing of up to:
explanation: The manual states a school bus can have up to a three-foot tail swing, requiring drivers to check mirrors during turning movements.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-11

question: A school bus should never be backed up when:
choice_d: Students are outside of the bus
explanation: The manual states you should never back a school bus when students are outside of the bus.
source_note: Alaska CDL Manual (AAMVA 2005 CDL Testing System, Version: July 2017, rev. AK DMV 02/2018), Section 10 - School Buses, p. 10-11
